text.p: The Philippines' largest conglomerate, Ayala Corp, is set to expand its business empire by investing in infrastructure-related projects, Ayala chairman Jaime Zobel de Ayala said on Tuesday.

"We have been greatly encouraged by the chance to expand our core businesses into new terrain. We have looked at the opportunities. We have weighed the risks and challenges. And we have chosen to be engaged," Ayala told a group of businessmen.
He said new investments in areas such as transportation, roads and water services would complement the conglomerate's existing businesses.
Ayala said the company had already invested in an elevated rail mass transit project that would pass through Manila's main thoroughfare.

It had also submitted an unsolicited proposal to build a $461-million railway that would connect Manila to its southern neighbours, Laguna and Batangas. And it had expressed interest in joining the privatisation of Manila's water supply system.

Ayala said its banking subsidiaries, Bank of the Philippine Islands, and its investment banking arm, BPI Capital Corp, would form a venture capital company that eight local companies have been invited to join.

"In exactly the same way that we have climbed out of the hole of the stagnation, so will we continue to move forward -- through the liberalisation and privatisation of economic effort. Only these can ensure the continued overall growth in our economy," he added.
